newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Melbourne airport says would nurture cheap airline.
newsitem.headline: Melbourne airport says would nurture cheap airline.

text.p: Melbourne airport owner, Asia Pacific Airports (APA), said on Wednesday it would be prepared to foster the development of a low-cost domestic carrier in Australia to boost its own business.

"If we see either an existing carrier that wants to start a new route or a new carrier entirely then we are happy to sit down with them and discuss how we can share some of the start-up risks that they face," Melbourne airport chief executive Terry Morgan told a luncheon hosted by the Committee for Economic Development of Australia (CEDA).

Morgan, formerly the managing director of London's Stansted airport, said Stansted had used this strategy successfully to aid the growth of the Irish low-cost airline, Ryanair, which operates regular services to Dublin.

"In any one year they (Ryanair) carry the entire population of Dublin in and out of Dublin. They have created that market from virtually zero and it is a formula that could be transferred across here," he said.
Morgan said the experience in Europe was that low-cost airline operators expanded the passenger market rather than taking market share away from the existing operators.
APA had assumed no new carriers in its growth projection for Melbourne airport over the next five years, Morgan said.
"But we are clearly trying to beat that," he said.

The APA group comprises British airport operator, BAA Plc with an initial 25.1 percent stake, insurance and funds group AMP Society with 49.9 percent and Sydney-based funds manager, Deutsche Bank AG's Axiom, with 25 percent.
BAA's stake would fall to 15.1 percent if a proposed fourth partner, Melbourne-based Hastings Fund Management, exercised an option to take a 10 percent interest.
